rainmeterSectionFlags.note: DynamicWindowSize=1 means the window/canvas auto-fits the union of all meter bounding boxes (including hidden ones per Rainmeter's normal relative-positioning rules) -- the background shape height formula depends on this.

importantColorNuance: The threshold-triggered 'over limit' font color is set via [!SetOptionGroup ... FontColor "#colorRed#,#colorTextAlpha#"] -- it reuses colorTextAlpha (205), NOT colorRedAlpha (255). So the red warning text renders at alpha 205, same as normal text, not fully opaque.

backgroundSpec.coordSystem: All numbers below are UNSCALED skin-space px; multiply by #Scale# (1.7) at the very end per the formulas (this mirrors Rainmeter's TransformationMatrix=Scale;0;0;Scale;Scale;Scale which scales around origin (Scale,Scale)).
backgroundSpec.overallH_note: Dynamic: MeterBackgroundHeight is an invisible 1px-tall helper Image meter placed after the last process row at Y=(BottomMargin+BgOffset)R = 8R past the prior meter's bottom. Its resolved absolute Y (unscaled) IS the total unscaled content height; multiplying by Scale gives the final background pixel height. In a from-scratch renderer, replace this indirection with: contentHeight = (title row height) + sum(visible row heights + RowSpacing gaps) + BottomMargin + BgOffset, all unscaled, then * Scale.

shapes.resolved_unscaled: Rectangle x=5, y=5, w=196, h=21, cornerRadius=4
shapes.purpose: Rounded-corner header/title band (top strip behind 'TOP CPU' title + process count row).
Squares off the bottom edge of the rounded top rect so only the TOP two corners stay rounded (Shape3 = Combine Shape | Union Shape2).
The larger rounded-corner body panel behind the process rows; height auto-extends to fill the rest of the dynamic window height.

Squares off the top edge of the body rect so only the BOTTOM two corners stay rounded (Shape6 = Combine Shape4 | Union Shape5). Net effect of Shape3+Shape6 stacked = one pill-ish rounded rectangle broken into a header capsule and a body capsule that visually overlap/abut around y=21-29 (unscaled) to look like a single continuous rounded panel.

shapes.formula: Rectangle ((BgShapeX-0.5)*Scale), ((BgShapeY-0.5)*Scale), ((BgShapeW+1)*Scale), (([MeterBackground:H]+Scale) - ((BgShapeX*2)*Scale)), ((CornerRadius+0.5)*Scale) | StrokeWidth (Stroke_Width*Scale) | Stroke Color StrokeColor,StrokeColorAlpha | Fill Color 0,0,0,0
shapes.CRITICAL_NOTE: Stroke_Width is the GLOBAL default from Variables.inc = 0 (only the 'r' recovery/alt theme variant redefines rStroke_Width=1). Neither TopCPU.ini nor TopRAM.ini override Stroke_Width in their [Variables] section (both only do @IncludeVariables/@IncludeStyles with no overrides). Therefore StrokeWidth evaluates to 0*1.7=0, meaning Shape7's outline is INVISIBLE in the currently-configured skin (fill is transparent 0,0,0,0 and stroke width is 0). Net visible effect: there is NO drawn border/frame around the panel -- only the two fill capsules (Shape3 top, Shape6 bottom) are visible. Flag this to the user/implementer since it's easy to assume a visible outline exists.

backgroundSpec.combineOps: Shape3 = Combine Shape | Union Shape2 (top capsule). Shape6 = Combine Shape4 | Union Shape5 (bottom capsule). Shape7 stands alone as the (currently invisible) frame. Group=Background.

measures.name: MeasureProcessCount
notes: Total count of running processes on the system, unrelated to the top-N list. Rendered top-right of the title bar as a bare number (see MeterProcessCount).

Threshold measure's own numeric value is never displayed directly; it exists purely to drive the group-wide FontColor of the row's Left(name) and Right(%) meters (Group=TopNCpu) based on whether the CPU% >= 20.

MeasureTopNCpuRam.name: [MeasureTopNCpu]
MeasureTopNCpuRam.note: Chains to the SAME process identified by MeasureTopNCpu (Name=[MeasureTopNCpu]) to fetch that process's RAM usage in bytes.

notes: Pure passthrough Calc (no IfConditions); exists only to decouple the OnChangeAction chain from the plugin measure. This is the measure actually read by MeterTopNCpuRam.

measures.effectiveNote: Given the resolved NumberOfTopCpuProc=5, rows 1-5 have UpdateDivider=1 (Disabled=0/false) and rows 6-10 have UpdateDivider=-1 & Disabled=1/true (i.e. rows 6-10 never run/update given current config). Only rows 1-5 are functionally live.

meters.name: MeterTop2CpuString .. MeterTop10CpuString / MeterTopNCpuRam / MeterTopNCpu (right)

y.note: R = stacks below the previous meter's bottom edge (the row-N-1 right/% meter, since that's the last meter defined before this one in the file) by (prevBottom + n). n=RowSpacing(1) if this row is populated, else n=0 (zero extra gap, but the row still occupies its own natural text-line height in the stack -- see verticalFlowSummary caveat).

meters.effectiveNote: With NumberOfTopCpuProc=5: rows 1-5 Hidden=false and render; rows 6-10 Hidden=true (and their backing measures are Disabled=true), so they never display given the current config. A from-scratch renderer targeting this exact configuration only needs to implement 5 rows, but the row-count is a variable (NumberOfTopCpuProc, 1-10 supported) in the original skin design.

verticalFlowSummary: Background capsule (unscaled y=5..~) -> Title row 'TOP CPU' centered at y=9 (abs) with process-count integer right-aligned same row -> Row1 (name/ram/cpu%) at y=32 (abs, TopMarginFormula) -> Rows 2-5 each stack below the previous row's bottom edge + RowSpacing(1) via Y=1R chaining (R = prevMeter.Y + prevMeter.H + n) -> Rows 6-10 exist in the file but are Hidden+Disabled given NumberOfTopCpuProc=5, stacking with 0 extra gap (Y=0R) directly atop row 5's bottom -> MeterBackgroundHeight (invisible) sits 8px (BottomMargin+BgOffset) below the last meter drawn (row 10's rightmost meter) and its resolved Y drives the background shape's total height.
notes: CAVEAT (hidden-meter stacking): Rainmeter's R/r relative-position resolution uses the immediately-preceding meter's resolved X/Y/W/H regardless of that meter's Hidden state -- hidden meters still occupy layout space equal to their natural (auto or explicit) height. Since rows 6-10 are always Hidden+Disabled under the given fixed variables (NumberOfTopCpuProc=5), and their own Y=0R (no added gap) references the prior row, they should stack with zero visual gap directly under row 5, adding no extra visible height beyond their own single text-line height repeated 5 times. HOWEVER, because a String meter's own H auto-sizes to its text bounding box (~ single line at 8pt Trebuchet MS Bold, no explicit H set on these meters), this could still add non-zero invisible height to the dynamic window/background if the renderer computes bounding boxes the same way Rainmeter does. Recommend either (a) verifying this empirically against a live Rainmeter render at NumberOfTopCpuProc=5, or (b) simply hard-coding a 5-row layout for this configuration and treating rows 6-10 as unused/dead code, since the resolved variable value never varies within this extraction.

Row line height is font-metric-dependent: Rainmeter (GDI+/DirectWrite text engine) auto-sizes each String meter's H to the natural line height of Trebuchet MS Bold at 8pt (times TransformationMatrix Scale=1.7). No fixed pixel value is given in the ini. A pixel-perfect Direct2D/DirectWrite reimplementation should measure this using the same font/size/weight rather than assume a constant, then apply RowSpacing(1 unscaled)=1.7px gaps between rows as per the Y=1R formula.

Column X positions (unscaled, multiply by Scale=1.7 for final px): Left/name = 7 (ContentMarginFormula), Center/RAM = 103 (CenterAlign), Right/CPU% = 197 (RightAlign). Row1's Left meter has an explicit W=70 (clip width) -- other columns are unconstrained width (auto-fit to formatted text) but positioned by their StringAlign anchor.

Text formats: process name = raw string from UsageMonitor (Substitute empty->'---' only); RAM column = '<value autoscaled to 1 decimal><K|M|G>B' e.g. '80.9MB'; CPU% column = '<value to 1 decimal>%' e.g. '4.8%'.

UsageMonitor plugin usage: primary CPU measures use Category/Counter implicitly via Alias=CPU + Index=N (Index selects the Nth-ranked process by that Alias's metric) plus Blacklist=#TopCpuBlacklist# (_Total|Idle) to exclude aggregate/idle pseudo-processes; the paired RAM measure for the same row instead uses Name=[MeasureTopNCpu] (chaining to the already-resolved process identity of the CPU measure) with Alias=RAM and NO Index/Blacklist of its own, ensuring it reports RAM for the exact same process the CPU column identified (not independently re-ranked by RAM).

Threshold-based coloring: TopCPUThreshold=20 (percent). A row's Left+Right text (Group=TopNCpu) switches from colorText(0,0,0/205) to colorRed(204,0,0) at alpha 205 (not 255) when that row's CPU% >= 20. The center RAM column is never threshold-colored -- always colorText2 (60,65,62/205).

Group=Controls meters (ControlSettings_, ControlSettings) are hover-reveal UI chrome (settings gear icon + its click region) unrelated to the data display; excluded from the meters list per instructions, see 'skipped'.
Only TopCPU (not TopRAM) has a MeasureProcessCount / MeterProcessCount / MeterProcessCountMouseRegion -- the total running-process count and its tooltip are unique to this panel.
